description: We are a team of software engineers fascinated by space, driven by curiosity to explore the universe, and passionate about learning more about the mysteries beyond our planet. We dream of one day being part of that exploration.
summary:
Marswalk is an interactive 3D map and Marswalk planner for future astronauts exploring Jezero Crater. It layers NASA orbital imagery (CTX, HiRISE), topography (MOLA/HRSC), thermal infrared (THEMIS) and spectral observation footprints (CRISM) with the Perseverance rover's real traverse on one globe.

From a terrain model built on the CTX digital elevation model, it computes a slope and roughness hazard map and plans the safest and most direct walking routes to science targets, with travel time, an elevation profile and an 8-hour EVA time budget. A Guide Mode then simulates the walk step by step with navigation cues.

Existing tools such as Mars Trek are built for regional and global views. Marswalk focuses on the hyperlocal scale of a single surface excursion, where crew safety and science return are decided.
details:
What it does. Marswalk lets a crew pick a science target in Jezero Crater, see it in context across several NASA data layers, and plan a safe walking route to it and back.

Layers. Viking MDIM 2.1 color context; MRO CTX (6 m/px) and HiRISE (25 cm/px) orthomosaics; MOLA + HRSC blended elevation with hillshade; THEMIS day and night thermal infrared; CRISM targeted-observation footprints; the Perseverance traverse, landing ellipse and waypoints. Each layer has a toggle, opacity control and a legend. Geological points of interest open a detail panel with imagery and context.

Hazard map. Slope (Horn method) and roughness (RMS deviation from a fitted plane over 60 m) are computed from the 20 m CTX DTM and aggregated to a 40 m grid. Cells are classed Low (<10°), Medium (10–18°), High (18–25°) or No-go (≥25°), thresholds informed by Apollo EVA experience.

Route planner. An A* search (8-connected, cost = 3D distance × (1 + λ·risk)) runs in a Web Worker and returns two options: Safest and Most direct. Paths are straightened where a straight line doesn't cross riskier ground. Travel time uses Tobler's hiking function rescaled to 2.5 km/h for a suited astronaut. A mission summary adds time at the site plus the return walk and checks it against an 8-hour EVA limit.

Guide Mode. A simulated walk along the planned route shows phase (walking out, science at site, walking back), position, heading, elapsed time and hazard cues, so a crew can rehearse the EVA.

How it's built. Next.js 15 and React 19 static export, CesiumJS on the Mars ellipsoid, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS. Raster tiles stream directly from NASA Mars Trek, so there is no tile-hosting cost. Python and Node scripts fetch NASA vector data and build the terrain grid. Hosted on Cloudflare Workers.

Benefits and goals. One integrated, hyperlocal view instead of switching between tools; route choices that trade safety against distance; realistic time budgets. The design generalizes to any site with a DTM and Mars Trek coverage.

Limitations. Rocks smaller than the 20 m DTM are not detected (HiRISE can be used to inspect a route). Travel times are hypothetical estimates, not validated human-performance data.
